(2), attention/PEPS transitions at beta=1/2 and kappa=2, Zwick mu*=1/2, sparse triangle 18/13, (3k+r)-clique formulas with unique K=5 saturation, Dominance e*=(13-sqrt(7))/4 in (2.5885, 2.5886), C3=2, C4=7/3, and k-gon limit 4*pi/(3*sqrt(3)). novelty.basis: Reframes OpenAI's rectangular exponent [5, 6] via the harmonic-reciprocal law (2) and systematically derives exact phase diagrams across self-attention, 2D PEPS, fine-grained graph problems, and Pythagorean tensor pricing, including e*=(13-sqrt(7))/4 for Dominance Product and the regular k-gon oscillation envelope. However, once Eq. (1) is given, the downstream derivations are elementary algebra and one-variable calculus.

reproducibility.basis: Specifies exact rational parameterizations, cleared-denominator Lean 4 theorem statements (Table 1), certified rational brackets, and 16 exact-Q certificate expectations (Table 2) with explicit runtime and adversarial test categories. Because code and certificates reside externally, independent verification of Lean 4 build status, verifier soundness, and timings is outside the PDF itself.

rigor.basis: Algebraic proofs of Theorems 2.1, 2.2, and 2.3(1–2) are clear, and Table 1 accurately summarizes 18 cleared-denominator Lean 4 identities. However, Theorem 2.1 declares rational domains Q_{>0}/Q_{>=1} while taking real derivatives, Theorem 2.3(3) analyzes irrational regular k-gons despite its Q^2 hypothesis, Theorem 2.5 asserts verifier soundness without a proof in the PDF, and Theorems 2.1–2.2 rely unconditionally on unrefereed preprints [5, 6].

significance.basis: Conditional on [5, 6], cleanly resolves exact arithmetic complexity exponents and zero-penalty saturation thresholds across nine benchmark problems, pinpointing d=sqrt(N) in attention, chi_B=chi^2 in 2D PEPS, K=5 among balanced tripartite cliques, and exact irrational Dominance Product improvement over 21/8. Utility is bounded by galactic fast-MM constants (noted in Sec. 5) and first-order scope of mean-width ratios.

potential_errors: Figure 3(a) plotting error: the marker labeled 'Dual / Zwick (1, 1, 1/2)' is plotted on the curve z = y/(1+y) at roughly (y ≈ 0.67, z = 0.40) instead of its actual normalized coordinates (y = b/a = 1.0, z = c/a = 0.5).

Theorem 2.3 quantifier/domain mismatch: the theorem statement restricts to sites P ⊂ Q^2 with exact rational pairwise distances and rational ratio ρ ∈ Q_{>0}, yet Part 3 analyzes unit-weight regular k-gons on the unit circle, which have irrational side lengths/ratios (e.g., ρ_4 = 8 - 4√2, ρ_6 = 4/√3) and no Q^2 embedding with rational distances for general k.

Theorem 2.1 domain vs. differentiability mismatch: Part 2 declares β ∈ Q_{>0} and Part 3 declares κ ∈ Q_{≥1} (matching Lean 4 rational arithmetic), yet both claim C^1-smoothness and second derivatives ω''_attn(1/2^±) and ω''_PEPS(2^-), which strictly require extending the piecewise formulas to R.

Theorem 2.1 notation slip: introduces weights a, b, c ∈ Q_{>0} with sorted order x ≥ y ≥ z > 0 without explicitly stating {x, y, z} = {a, b, c} or the permutation symmetry ω(F; a, b, c) = ω(F; x, y, z) used when evaluating ω(F; 1, β, 1) for β < 1.

Theorem 2.5 ('Soundness and Anti-Forgery Design of NINE-FOURTHS-PHASE-CERT-1.0') is presented as a theorem in Section 2.4 without a proof in the PDF, functioning instead as a summary of the external Python script's checks paired with empirical test counts in Section 4.2.
strengths: Every algebraic identity, closed-form exponent, derivative jump, rational bracket, and penalty value in Theorems 2.1–2.3 and Tables 1–2 is algebraically sound and internally consistent (e.g., ω_attn(1/2+δ)-2 = 2δ^2/(1+2δ) with ω''(1/2^+)=4; κ_c=2 for 2D PEPS; Zwick APSP μ*=1/2; sparse triangle 18/13; exact (3k+r)-clique spectrum with unique K=5 saturation; Dominance Product e*=(13-√7)/4 ∈ (5177/2000, 12943/5000) beating 21/8; Pythagorean C_3=2 and C_4=7/3).

Clean harmonic-reciprocal reformulation (Eq. 2) that unifies zero-penalty saturation across rectangular shapes via x^-1 + y^-1 ≤ z^-1 and cleanly explains second-order phase transitions in self-attention and 2D PEPS.
Transparent scoping in Section 5 and Remark 2.4 acknowledging galactic fast-MM constant overheads and distinguishing first-order mean-width ratios from full asymptotic tensor rank for k ≥ 4 cycles.
Clear visual alignment across Figures 1, 2, and 3(b), including exact match of the (3k+r)-clique penalty bars (K=3..18) and the period-3 regular k-gon oscillation envelope converging to 4π/(3√3).
strong_novelty_candidates: Exact quadratic algebraic exponent e* = (13 - √7)/4 ≈ 2.588562 (minimal polynomial 8e^2 - 52e + 81 = 0) for rectangular All-Pairs Dominance Product under ω_F = 9/4, strictly improving Matoušek's square-MM bound 21/8 = 2.625.

Exact C^1-smooth second-order phase transitions for Transformer self-attention at d_c = √N (β_c = 1/2, ω''(1/2^+) = 4) and 2D PEPS boundary contraction at χ_B = χ^2 (κ_c = 2, ω''(2^-) = 1/2), plus uniqueness of K = 5 as the sole zero-penalty saturated balanced tripartite K-clique (K ≥ 3).

Exact-Q Pythagorean Euclidean mean-width capacity ratios for 3-cycle (2) and 3×4 PEPS plaquette C_4 (7/3), together with the regular k-gon convergence and period-3 oscillation characterization around 4π/(3√3).
summary: Conditional on the cited November 24, 2026 OpenAI preprints [5, 6] establishing ω_F = 9/4, α_F = 1/2, and the closed-form rectangular matrix multiplication exponent (1), the paper systematically derives exact complexity phase diagrams and zero-penalty saturation criteria across Transformer self-attention, 2D PEPS boundary contraction, fine-grained graph/parsing algorithms, and first-order Euclidean mean-width tensor pricing. All main algebraic identities, closed-form exponents (including Zwick APSP 5/2, sparse triangle 18/13, balanced tripartite (3k+r)-clique with unique K=5 saturation, and Dominance Product e* = (13-√7)/4), rational brackets, and regular k-gon limits (4π/(3√3)) are mathematically verified from the proofs and consistent with Tables 1–2 and Figures 1–2 and 3(b). Minor presentation and rigor defects—most notably a misplotted marker for Dual/Zwick (1, 1, 1/2) in Figure 3(a), Part 3 of Theorem 2.3 exceeding the Q^2/rational-distance hypothesis stated in the preamble, real derivatives taken on functions declared on Q in Theorem 2.1, an unproved 'Theorem 2.5' describing an external verifier, and unconditional phrasing of premises from [5, 6]—do not invalidate the core derived theorems.
weaknesses: Downstream mathematical steps from Eq. (1) in Theorems 2.1–2.2 consist largely of straightforward algebraic substitutions and one-variable calculus, and all complexity claims inherit unverified dependence on the same-week external preprints [5, 6] without explicit conditional framing.

The Lean 4 formalization (Table 1) verifies 18 cleared-denominator algebraic identities rather than the algorithmic complexity reductions (e.g., Zwick APSP, Matoušek dominance product, Alon–Yuster–Zwick) or the compactness/Jensen proof in Theorem 2.3(3).

Minor rigor and presentation issues: misplotted 'Dual / Zwick (1, 1, 1/2)' point in Figure 3(a), Theorem 2.3(3) stepping outside Q^2, Theorem 2.1 differentiating functions stated on Q, and Theorem 2.5 lacking a proof in the PDF.
External artifacts (Lean 4 files, Python verifier, 16 JSON certificates, and 48 adversarial tests) cannot be independently executed or audited from the PDF alone.
